title: v1.0 scope claims ~38 modules; only 22 are registered
repro: grep -c import src/modules/index.ts (22 module imports at lines 3-27) vs docs/BLUEPRINT.md TL;DR (L20) "~38 modules"
notes: No recorded decision trims the module count. A public 0.9.0 release described against this TL;DR overstates scope by ~42%. Smallest fix: either land the missing ~16 modules or correct the TL;DR/locked-decisions count to the real number so the release description is honest.

title: Org/product domains (vysted.com, terminal.vysted.com) do not resolve
repro: curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://vysted.com and https://terminal.vysted.com -> both exit 6 (could not resolve host)
evidence: docs/BLUEPRINT.md:31-32 (domain structure); DNS lookup failure for both hosts
notes: Expected pre-launch, but the BLUEPRINT.md claim reads as a current fact ("vysted.com IS the org/lab landing page") rather than a plan. Smallest fix: register + park a minimal landing page before a public 0.9.0 announcement, or soften the doc's tense to future/planned.

title: Locked UI stack still names Next.js 16; the shipped bundler is Vite
repro: grep next package.json -> no match; package.json:8 "dev": "vite", :82 vite ^8.0.16
evidence: package.json:8,82; docs/BLUEPRINT.md:52 (Locked Decisions table still says "Tauri 2.x + Next.js 16 + TypeScript + Tailwind 4 + shadcn/ui"); docs/redesign/DECISIONS.md:28 (D6, the Vite migration decision)
notes: D6 authorized the migration and the license line at BLUEPRINT.md:8/:58 was corrected in place for its own decision (D83) — the stack line at :52 never got the same treatment. A Tier-1 "Locked" document describing its own architecture incorrectly is exactly the kind of drift that erodes trust in a research-lab-voice public release. Smallest fix: one-line edit to BLUEPRINT.md:52/:14 swapping Next.js 16 for Vite, citing D6.

title: OpenBB data layer no longer matches its locked "wrapped as a runtime sidecar" description
repro: sidecar/requirements.txt:32-36 comment: "the retired Phase-2 OpenBB Tier-2 plugin is gone in v0.4.0; its data surface is preserved through openbb-mcp" (a separate subprocess, not an in-process wrap)
evidence: sidecar/requirements.txt:32-36; sidecar/openbb_mcp_subprocess/; sidecar/services/openbb_mcp_provider.py; docs/BLUEPRINT.md:55,84 (still says "wrapped as a runtime sidecar")
notes: Provider breadth is preserved so this is not a functional gap, but the architecture description is stale in a Locked doc, same class of issue as the Vite drift above. Smallest fix: update BLUEPRINT.md:55/:84 to describe the openbb-mcp subprocess architecture.

title: Distribution promise (SignPath signing, Homebrew cask, GitHub Releases) is unbuilt; CI ships unsigned bundles
repro: grep -rli signpath .github/workflows scripts -> 0 hits; .github/workflows/build.yml:76 step name "Build Tauri bundle (unsigned)"; gh release list -> empty; no Homebrew formula/cask file anywhere in the repo
notes: Auto-updater plugin and AppImage bundle target are wired; signing and cask distribution are not. This is normal for pre-0.9.0 but would block an actual public release as promised (users would get SmartScreen/Gatekeeper warnings with no bypass docs shipped either). Smallest fix: track as an explicit release-blocking TODO with an owner, not silently assumed done.

title: Rust layer never built a system tray
evidence: src-tauri/tauri.conf.json (no trayIcon config); src-tauri/src/lib.rs (623 lines, window lifecycle + sidecar/MCP spawn + keychain + kill-switch, no tray setup)
notes: Windowing and OS integration (the other two thirds of this promise) are real and substantial. Tray is a named sub-feature with zero implementation, not a partial attempt. Smallest fix: either implement a minimal tray (status icon + quit) or drop the claim from BLUEPRINT.md §3.1.

title: "Rust layer provides file system access" is not implemented — no fs permission, CSV export bypasses native fs entirely
repro: cat src-tauri/capabilities/default.json -> permissions = [core:default, global-shortcut:allow-is-registered, notification:default, shell:allow-open], no fs:*; grep tauri-plugin-fs src-tauri/Cargo.toml package.json -> 0 hits
evidence: src-tauri/capabilities/default.json:6-11; src/modules/portfolio/PortfolioPanel.tsx:9,504 (imports downloadCsv from src/lib/csv.ts, a webview Blob/anchor download, not a Tauri fs write)
notes: The only file-writing user flow in the product today (portfolio CSV export) never touches Rust at all. If a future feature (e.g. workspace import/export to a chosen path, or writing research briefs to disk) assumes this capability exists per BLUEPRINT.md §3.1, it will discover there is no fs permission granted. Smallest fix: either grant a scoped fs:* capability + wire a real save-to-path flow, or correct the promise to describe the current browser-download mechanism.
